biography: Step into wonder and find your inner explorer with National Geographic 🌎

latestPosts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Africa Earth’s Wild Home, narrated by @wunmimosaku, premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on National Geographic. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Many orphaned giant anteater pups in Brazil are still nursing when their mothers are killed in road collisions. At rehabilitation centers, caregivers bottle-feed them, provide around-the-clock care, and help them build strength for a possible return to the wild. Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spent three years documenting these young animals and the people caring for them.

See how researchers are making Brazil's roads safer for giant anteaters at the link in bio.

In the Alaska Peninsula, a brown bear surrounds a school of sockeye salmon that had journeyed thousands of miles upstream to the freshwaters of Alaska from the Pacific Ocean. Photographer @mikerigney told National Geographic this salmon migration was "easily one of the most beautiful natural displays I've ever seen."

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and other forms of dementia don't occur overnight. Up to a decade before memory impairment appears, subtle cognitive symptoms can emerge. While these signs alone aren't definitive, recognizing patterns can help patients and families prepare for what lies ahead.

Learn more about these signs and what experts say patients and their families can do at the link in bio.

Presented by @Rolex. Hunted for their scales and meat, pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with millions believed to have been harvested in Africa over recent decades. But in places like Cameroon, conservationists are working to protect these armored creatures. At the @tikkihywoodfoundation's rescue center, staff and minders tend to injured pangolins before rehabilitating them for release into the wild, managing complex care needs that can change from day to day.
